ucs.title: [LLM] Akira pre-encryption recovery inhibition — PowerShell WMI shadow-copy wipe → mass .akira rename
ucs.description: Hunts Akira's signature recovery-inhibition one-liner (Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy | Remove-WmiObject) immediately preceding mass file encryption with the .akira/.powerranges extension. This exact PowerShell-WMI shadow-deletion technique is documented for Akira/GOLD SAHARA/PUNK SPIDER (Howling Scorpius, G1024) in CISA AA24-109A and is distinct from the vssadmin form used by most crews.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe OR Processes.process_name=cmd.exe) (Processes.process="*Win32_Shadowcopy*" OR Processes.process="*Win32_ShadowCopy*") (Processes.process="*Remove-WmiObject*" OR Processes.process="*Remove-CimInstance*" OR Processes.process="*.Delete()*" OR Processes.process="*delete()*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename dest as host | where user!="*$" | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "Win32_Shadowcopy"   // Akira AA24-109A signature object
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Remove-WmiObject","Remove-CimInstance",".Delete()","delete()")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
| where CommandLine has "Win32_Shadowcopy"
| where CommandLine has_any ("Remove-WmiObject","Remove-CimInstance",".Delete()","delete()")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Akira Ransomware Shadow Copy Deletion via PowerShell WMI
id: 9e1f3b2a-7c64-4d2e-9b3a-akira-shadowcopy
status: experimental
description: Detects Akira (G1024) signature recovery-inhibition one-liner deleting VSS shadow copies via Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy | Remove-WmiObject
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  selection_obj:
    CommandLine|contains: 'Win32_Shadowcopy'
  selection_action:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Remove-WmiObject'
      - 'Remove-CimInstance'
      - '.Delete()'
      - 'delete()'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_obj and selection_action
falsepositives:
  - Rare legitimate backup/admin scripts that prune shadow copies via WMI
level: high
tags:
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.t1059.001
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE) @CommandLine:(*Win32_Shadowcopy* OR *Win32_ShadowCopy*) @CommandLine:(*Remove-WmiObject* OR *Remove-CimInstance* OR *delete\(\)*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)Win32_Shadowcopy", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(?i)(Remove-WmiObject|Remove-CimInstance|\.[Dd]elete\(\))", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName], function=collect([CommandLine]))
ucs.rationale: Most ransomware deletes shadow copies via vssadmin/wmic; Akira's published playbook (AA24-109A) specifically uses the PowerShell WMI object Win32_Shadowcopy piped to Remove-WmiObject. Anchoring on that exact object+cmdlet pair makes this near-unique to Akira/Howling Scorpius rather than a generic T1490 template, while remaining resilient to renamed binaries via case-insensitive matching.

ucs.title: [LLM] Akira hands-on-keyboard staging — remote-access tool + bulk exfil utility co-located on one host
ucs.description: Hunts Akira's characteristic post-compromise toolset: deploying a remote-access tool (AnyDesk/RustDesk/LedgerSMB-style) for persistence alongside a bulk exfiltration utility (rclone/WinSCP/FileZilla/MEGAsync) on the same host before encryption. This dual-use tool pairing is a documented PUNK SPIDER/GOLD SAHARA tradecraft signature and rarely co-occurs benignly.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count values(Processes.process_name) as tools min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("anydesk.exe","rustdesk.exe","screenconnect.exe","rclone.exe","winscp.exe","filezilla.exe","megasync.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval rat=if(match(tools,"anydesk|rustdesk|screenconnect"),1,0), exfil=if(match(tools,"rclone|winscp|filezilla|megasync"),1,0) | where rat=1 AND exfil=1 | where user!="*$" | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
let Lookback = 14d;
let RAT = dynamic(["anydesk.exe","rustdesk.exe","screenconnect.exe","connectwisecontrol.exe"]);
let Exfil = dynamic(["rclone.exe","winscp.exe","filezilla.exe","megasync.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where FileName in~ (RAT) or FileName in~ (Exfil)
   or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has_any ("AnyDesk","RustDesk","rclone","WinSCP","MEGA")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend ToolClass = case(FileName in~ (RAT), "RemoteAccess", FileName in~ (Exfil), "Exfil", "Other")
| summarize Classes = make_set(ToolClass), Tools = make_set(FileName),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, AccountName
| where set_has_element(Classes, "RemoteAccess") and set_has_element(Classes, "Exfil")
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let Lookback = 14d;
let RAT = dynamic(["anydesk.exe","rustdesk.exe","screenconnect.exe","connectwisecontrol.exe"]);
let Exfil = dynamic(["rclone.exe","winscp.exe","filezilla.exe","megasync.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend Bin = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where Bin in (RAT) or Bin in (Exfil)
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| extend ToolClass = case(Bin in (RAT), "RemoteAccess", Bin in (Exfil), "Exfil", "Other")
| summarize Classes = make_set(ToolClass), Tools = make_set(Bin),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by Computer, SubjectUserName
| where set_has_element(Classes, "RemoteAccess") and set_has_element(Classes, "Exfil")
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\anydesk.exe OR *\AnyDesk.exe OR *\rustdesk.exe OR *\RustDesk.exe OR *\screenconnect.exe OR *\rclone.exe OR *\WinSCP.exe OR *\winscp.exe OR *\filezilla.exe OR *\FileZilla.exe OR *\megasync.exe OR *\MEGAsync.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(anydesk|rustdesk|screenconnect|connectwisecontrol|rclone|winscp|filezilla|megasync)\.exe$/i
| ToolClass := if(regex("(?i)(anydesk|rustdesk|screenconnect|connectwisecontrol)", field=ImageFileName), then="RemoteAccess", else="Exfil")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=[collect([ToolClass]), collect([ImageFileName])])
| regex("RemoteAccess", field=ToolClass) | regex("Exfil", field=ToolClass)
ucs.rationale: Any one of these tools alone is noisy (IT uses AnyDesk and rclone legitimately). Akira's tradecraft is the co-location of an unsanctioned remote-access tool AND a bulk-transfer utility under the same operator account on one host within the intrusion window — the double-extortion staging pattern CISA and Mandiant attribute to GOLD SAHARA.
